headline: SOUTH32 $2B HERMOSA MINE GETS USFS FINAL ROD — 5 CRITICAL MINERALS CLEARED FOR ARIZONA, FULL PRODUCTION BY 2029
snippet: The US Forest Service issued its Final Record of Decision on July 7, completing NEPA review for South32's Hermosa mine infrastructure on Coronado National Forest land in southern Arizona — approving the primary access road, dry-stack tailings facility, and a portion of a 138kV power line. Hermosa is one of the few US projects capable of producing five federally designated critical minerals simultaneously (zinc, silver, manganese, copper, and lead) and is targeted to reach full production by 2029.

headline: DAKOTA GOLD COMPLETES 112-HOLE RICHMOND HILL PFS DRILL — 77.19 G/T AU OVER 3.2M IN STEP-OUT, PFS DUE Q4 (NYSE:DC)
snippet: Dakota Gold (NYSE American: DC) has wrapped its 2026 pre-feasibility study drill campaign at Richmond Hill in South Dakota's Homestake Belt — 17,273 metres across 112 holes — with standout expansion hole RH26C-432 returning 11.36 g/t Au over 26.3m including 77.19 g/t Au over 3.2m, located approximately 365m north of the current measured and indicated resource boundary. All 2025–2026 drill data now feeds into a Pre-Feasibility Study due Q4 2026, with high-grade Deadwood Formation intercepts in the Northern Expansion area growing the resource footprint ahead of that economic milestone.

headline: FIRST DRILL TURNS AT WHISTLER: U.S. GOLDMINING FIRES 6,000M ON $2B NPV ALASKA GOLD-COPPER PORPHYRY (NASDAQ:USGO)
snippet: U.S. GoldMining Inc. (NASDAQ: USGO) activated the first drill at its 100%-owned Whistler Gold-Copper Project 105 miles northwest of Anchorage, Alaska on July 6 — a fully funded 6,000-metre program testing 8–10 highest-ranked targets within the Whistler Orbit, launched ahead of schedule. Whistler's 2024 PEA outlined an after-tax NPV5% of US$2.0 billion and 33% IRR at base-case prices of US$3,200/oz gold and US$4.50/lb copper — both materially below current spot — making discovery-phase results the defining catalyst for the company's valuation reset.

headline: TROILUS HITS 164M AT 0.95 G/T AUEQ IN UNSAMPLED Z87 PIT ZONES — 40,000M 2026 QUEBEC CAMPAIGN UNDERWAY (TSX:TLG)
snippet: Troilus Mining Corp. (TSX: TLG) released July 7 results from 7 holes totalling 1,845 metres in its Z87 pit optimization program at the Troilus Project in north-central Quebec — the headline intercept returned 0.83 g/t Au, 1.30 g/t Ag, and 0.06% Cu over 164 metres while testing historically unsampled intervals from 1970s drilling within the Z87 reserve pit shell. Troilus has now completed 5,563 metres of a dedicated 24,000-metre Z87 program targeting resource category upgrades on inferred material inside the pit shell, a key input for a future production decision at one of Quebec's largest undeveloped gold-copper deposits.

headline: PROSPECT RIDGE WINS EXCALIBUR BC PORPHYRY PERMIT — MAIDEN 3,000M ON NEVER-DRILLED 1KM×2KM BABINE IP ANOMALY (CSE:PRR)
source_name: PR Inside / Prospect Ridge Resources Corp.
snippet: Prospect Ridge Resources Corp. (CSE: PRR) secured a multi-year area-based drilling permit July 7 for its 100%-owned Excalibur copper-gold porphyry project in BC's Babine Belt — a 28 km² tenure near the former Huckleberry, Bell, and Granisle mines — with a maiden 3,000-metre discovery program planned for summer 2026 targeting a 1km × 2km geophysical anomaly that has never been drill-tested. The IP survey shows moderate chargeability flanked by high chargeability / low resistivity interpreted as a pyrite halo, plus a coincident magnetic high consistent with magnetite-rich potassic alteration — the textbook signatures of a copper-bearing calc-alkaline porphyry core.

headline: BP SILVER DRILLS PHASE 2 AT BOLIVIAN COSUÑO: 2,000M FOLLOWING 600 G/T AG DISCOVERY HIT IN POTOSÍ (TSXV:BPAG)
snippet: BP Silver Corp. (TSXV: BPAG) commenced its Phase 2 drill program at Cosuño in Bolivia's Potosí Department on June 30, with the first hole following up the Pocañita Chica target where Phase 1 returned 5m at 600.40 g/t Ag including 1m at 1,655 g/t Ag — the Phase 2 program is a 2,000-metre, 20–24 hole campaign within a broader 8,000m 2026 campaign designed to test the full scale of the Cosuño lithocap-hosted hydrothermal system. Lithocap systems overlying intermediate-sulphidation epithermal veins routinely host far larger silver deposits at depth than their surface expressions suggest, making Phase 2 a potential scale-defining event for Cosuño.

headline: WESTERN URANIUM SUNDAY MINE ASSAYS RUN 40%+ ABOVE PROBE GRADES — OUTSIZED FINAL PAYMENT FROM WHITE MESA MILL (CSE:WUC)
source_name: Resource World / Western Uranium & Vanadium Corp.
snippet: Western Uranium & Vanadium Corp. (CSE: WUC / OTCQX: WSTRF) announced July 6 that post-processing chemical assays of uranium ore delivered from its Sunday Mine Complex in Utah to Energy Fuels' White Mesa Mill came in more than 40% above the probe-indicated grades estimated at delivery, resulting in a materially larger final payment than initial invoices projected. CEO George Glasier described the grade outperformance as a 'strong testament to the quality' of Western's mineral resources at Sunday Mine — a result that reinforces the resource confidence at a mine feeding the only US facility capable of processing both uranium and rare earth elements in an integrated operation.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,168 AHEAD OF JULY 8 FOMC MINUTES — FIRST WEEKLY GAIN SINCE MAY AS FED RATE-HIKE BETS RECEDE
snippet: Gold spot held near $4,168 per ounce on July 7 — up roughly $23 from Monday and on track for its first weekly gain since May — as softer-than-expected June payroll data continued to reduce the probability of an imminent Fed rate hike and traders positioned ahead of the July 8 FOMC meeting minutes. The minutes will reveal how the June 9–9 no-change vote broke down — a dovish-leaning split would likely extend the metals' post-payrolls recovery, while a hawkish-reading majority would weigh disproportionately on junior mining equities relative to the metal.

headline: ANDY HOME: BATTERY METALS BOUNCE STALLS AS EV SALES GROWTH CRASHES TO 0.9% — CHINA MARKET DOWN 15% IN H1 2026
snippet: Reuters metals columnist Andy Home argues that the cyclical recovery in lithium, cobalt, and nickel prices — driven by DRC cobalt export restrictions and Indonesia's nickel quota cuts — is running into a structural headwind: after EV sales surged 20% year-on-year in 2025, global growth has slowed to just 0.9% in January–May 2026, with China sales down 15% and North America down 25% year-on-year. For investors in battery-metals juniors, the column draws a critical distinction between the supply-restraint rally (already priced in) and a demand-pull re-rating that the current EV sales data has not yet validated.

headline: COT GOLD: MANAGED MONEY HOLDS BELOW-PEAK NET-LONG AS SPECS SIT OUT REBOUND — DELAYED CFTC RELEASE JULY 6 ANALYZED
snippet: GoldSeek's July 6 COT analysis — based on the CFTC Commitments of Traders report delayed from Friday to Monday due to the US Independence Day holiday — examines speculative positioning in gold, silver, and the US dollar index ahead of Wednesday's FOMC minutes release. The report notes that managed money's net-long position in gold remains well below historical cycle-peak extremes, a positioning backdrop that has historically preceded the most sustained upside moves in both the metal and leveraged junior mining equities.

headline: PENTAGON DEALS AND PROCESSING BOTTLENECK: INVESTORNEWS CRITICAL MINERALS REPORT SEES NEXT PHASE OF SUPPLY CHAIN COMPETITION
snippet: InvestorNews' July 6 critical minerals roundup identifies the real strategic bottleneck in Western supply chains as having shifted from mine output to processing — with China controlling an estimated 94% of global rare earth magnet manufacturing capacity — as REalloys, Titan Mining, ioneer, and Energy Exploration Technologies all announced Department of Defense agreements in the latest reporting period. The report also flags Sweden's Norra Kärr heavy rare earth project as a single asset with the certified capacity to supply all of Europe's annual dysprosium requirements, identifying it as a proxy for the scale of non-Chinese separation capacity being targeted by Western policy.
